source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

06091.t:
Sierra County barely moved in the race for governor. Hilton (R) carried it 929 to 570 over Becerra (D), a margin of 24 points, almost exactly Trump's 24-point margin in 2024. The shift toward the Democrats rounds to zero, while California as a whole moved 10 points their way and the typical county in the state moved 6. Sierra ranks 54th of California's 58 counties by move and 57th by votes cast. Similar Republican-leaning counties moved further: Colusa by 17 points, Yuba by 10 and Mariposa by 3.

Turnout was 1,499 votes, 85% of the 1,754 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, these figures are close to final.

06041.t:
Marin County gave Becerra (D) a 59-point lead over Hilton (R) for governor, 54,621 votes to 14,019. That is 5 points less Democratic than Harris's 64-point margin in 2024. It was the only shift of that size in California, where 54 of 58 counties moved left and the typical county moved 6 points toward the Democrats. Marin ranked last of the 58 by move. Nearby San Francisco and Santa Cruz each moved about 4 points left, while San Mateo moved 2 points right.

Only 52% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 68,640 votes so far are 48% of the 2024 total. With turnout this far down, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06009.t:
In the governor's race, Calaveras County stayed firmly Republican and barely shifted. Hilton beat Becerra here 13,577 to 7,736, a 27-point margin, against Trump's 28-point win in 2024: a move of about 1 point toward the Democrats. Statewide the race swung 11 points left, and the typical California county moved 6 points; Calaveras ranks 51st of 58. Counties of similar size and lean split: Amador hardly moved, while Yuba and Sutter shifted 12 and 17 points left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout was 21,313 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the small shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from those who stayed home.

06107.t:
In the race for governor between Becerra and Hilton, Tulare County moved about 20 points toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 21 points in 2024; Hilton now leads by about one point, 50,741 votes to 49,902. That is the fifth-largest move among California's 58 counties, where the typical county moved 6 points and the state as a whole 11. Counties with similar 2024 results and size moved alike: Madera 17 points, Kings 19 and Kern 23, enough in Kern for a narrow Becerra lead.

Only 74.6% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 100,643 votes so far equal 73% of the 2024 total. With a drop that large, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06017.t:
In the governor's race between Becerra and Hilton, El Dorado County went Republican by 13 points, 53,032 votes to 40,798, slightly wider than Trump's 12-point margin over Harris in 2024. That one-point move toward the Republicans set it against the tide. Becerra won the state by 32 points, 54 of California's 58 counties moved left, and only one moved further right than El Dorado.

Comparable counties moved the other way: Placer shifted 3 points left, while Stanislaus and Tulare each swung about 17 to 19 points left. Turnout was 93,830, or 84% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06087.t:
Santa Cruz County voted for Becerra over Hilton for governor by 58 points, 90,275 to 23,799. That is 4 points more Democratic than its 54-point margin for Harris over Trump in 2024. The shift was smaller than the state's 11-point move, smaller than the typical California county's 6 points, and well short of the national typical move of 14. It ranks 38th of 58 counties in the state by move.

Among similar counties, Alameda moved 8 points and Sonoma 5, while San Mateo barely changed. About 114,000 votes were cast, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06023.t:
In the race for California governor, Humboldt County has so far voted for Becerra over Hilton 30,506 to 15,069, a Democratic margin of 34 points. Harris carried it by 28 in 2024, so the county moved about 6 points toward the Democrats. That is close to the typical move among California counties but well short of the state's 11-point shift. Among similar counties, Mendocino moved 9 points, Santa Barbara 6 and Monterey 11.

The 45,575 votes counted so far equal 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 92% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

06051.t:
In the governor's race, Mono County backed Becerra over Hilton by 22 points, 3,015 votes to 1,908, up from Harris's 20-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 2-point shift toward the Democrats is smaller than California's statewide move of 10 points and the typical county's 6, ranking Mono 47th of 58 counties. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Among similar California counties, San Benito moved 9 points and Mendocino 12, while Humboldt moved 4. Mono cast 4,923 votes, 81% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06065.t:
In the race for governor, Riverside County swung from a narrow Trump win in 2024 (R+1) to a 17-point margin for Becerra over Hilton, 390,385 votes to 278,471. That 18-point move toward the Democrats is larger than the state's 11-point shift and the typical California county's 6, and ranks seventh of 58. It is close to San Joaquin's 17 points, behind neighbouring San Bernardino's 21 and well ahead of Orange's 8. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points left.

Only 668,856 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With about 80% of the expected vote counted, these numbers may still move.

06071.t:
San Bernardino County swung hard toward the Democrats in the race for governor. Trump carried it by 2 points in 2024; Becerra won it over Hilton by 19, 362,375 votes to 248,239. That 21-point move is the third-largest of California's 58 counties, against a typical county move of 6 points and a statewide shift of 11. The county was one of 10 in the state to go from Trump to the Democrat. Its closest neighbours in size and 2024 vote, Riverside and San Joaquin, each moved 17 points, while Orange moved 6.

Turnout fell to 610,614 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06043.t:
Mariposa County moved about 3 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor, but Hilton still carried it comfortably over Becerra, 4,526 votes to 3,137, a Republican margin of 18 points. In 2024 Trump won it by 21 points.

That shift was smaller than in most of California, where 54 of 58 counties moved left and the typical county moved about 6 points. Statewide the swing was 10 points. Mariposa ranks 44th by move. It tracked Plumas (3 points) and Siskiyou (2) but lagged Del Norte (8). Turnout was 81% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06073.t:
San Diego County voted for Becerra over Hilton in the governor's race by 25 points, 751,199 to 448,688. In 2024 Harris carried it by 17, so the county moved 8 points toward the Democrats. That beats the typical California county's 6-point shift and ranks 22nd of 58, but it trails the statewide move of 11 and the national typical move of 14. Comparable counties moved about as much: Orange and Ventura by 8, Sacramento by 10.

Turnout fell to 81% of the 2024 vote, with 1,199,887 ballots counted. That drop is large enough that the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06089.t:
Shasta County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race, but by less than in 2024. With 74% of the expected vote counted, Hilton leads Becerra 38,840 to 20,038, a margin of about 32 points, against Trump's 37-point win over Harris. That is a shift of about 5 points toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical California county's 6 and well short of the statewide 11-point swing or the national typical 14. Similar counties moved more: Tehama 5, Glenn 7, Sutter 17.

The count so far, 58,878 votes, is 66% of Shasta's 2024 total, so the result cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With a quarter of the vote still out, the numbers may move.

06055.t:
Napa County backed Becerra over Hilton for governor by 39 points, 31,472 votes to 13,681. That is a 4-point move toward the Democrats from Harris's 35-point margin in 2024. Only 79.6% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move.

The shift is smaller than California's statewide move of 11 points and the typical county's 6. It ranks 35th of 58 counties. Similar counties moved more: Yolo shifted 9 points and Monterey 11, while Humboldt's 6-point move was close to Napa's. Turnout so far is 69% of the 2024 vote, 45,153 ballots against 65,549. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06037.t:
Los Angeles County gave Democrat Becerra a 46-point win over Republican Hilton in the governor's race, 2,229,512 votes to 817,323. That is a 13-point move toward the Democrats from Harris's 33-point margin in 2024, larger than the state's 11-point shift and more than double the typical California county's 6 points. It ranks 14th of 58 counties by move and first by votes cast. Similar large Democratic counties moved less: Contra Costa by 5 points, Santa Clara by 2. Monterey moved 10.

About 3,046,835 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06113.t:
In the governor's race between Becerra and Hilton, Yolo County moved about 10 points toward the Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential vote. Harris carried it by 36 points; Becerra leads by 46, with 40,936 votes to 15,025. That shift roughly matches the statewide move of 10 points and ranks 19th of California's 58 counties. It is well above the typical county move in the state (6 points) but below the national figure (14). Similar counties moved less, Napa and Contra Costa by about 5 points each, while Monterey moved about the same, 10.

Only 66% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 55,961 ballots so far equal 60% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06059.t:
Orange County moved about 8 points toward the Democrats in the governor's race between Becerra and Hilton. Harris carried it by 3 points in 2024. Becerra won it by about 11, 633,955 votes to 511,845. Turnout was 82% of the 2024 total, 1,145,800 votes against 1,390,965. With that drop, the count cannot tell how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters staying home.

06033.t:

In 2024 it narrowly backed Trump by 1 point on 26,759 votes, so this is a 13-point move toward the Democrats and one of 11 California counties to flip from Trump to the Democrat. 06111.t:

Turnout was 77% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Only 88% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move.

06115.t:

06035.t:

Lassen cast 8,889 votes, about 78% of its 2024 total of 11,371, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

The 179,498 votes counted so far equal 71% of the 2024 total, and only about 80% of the expected vote is in, so these numbers may still move. With turnout this far below 2024, the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06081.t:
San Mateo County gave Becerra a 51-point win over Hilton in the governor's race, 208,736 votes to 67,203. The county ranks 50th of 58 in California by move. The typical county moved 6 points left in the state and 14 nationally.

Counties with similar 2024 margins and size moved further: Sonoma and Santa Cruz each about 4 points, Alameda 8. The county cast 275,939 votes, 83% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06063.t:
In the governor's race, Plumas County stayed firmly Republican and moved only slightly toward the Democrats. Hilton beat Becerra 4,877 to 3,625, a margin of 15 points, compared with Trump's 17-point win here in 2024. That 2-point shift ranks 48th of California's 58 counties, well short of the typical county's 6 points, the state's 11-point swing toward Becerra and the 14-point move of the typical county nationally. It tracks similar counties nearby: Mariposa and Siskiyou each moved about 3 points, while Del Norte moved 6.

Turnout was 8,502 votes, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who switched sides from those who stayed home.

06047.t:
Merced County swung toward the Democrats in the race for governor, going from a 4-point Trump win in 2024 to a 16-point lead for Becerra over Hilton, 28,681 votes to 20,806. That 20-point move is the third largest among California's 58 counties, where the typical county moved 6 points left and the state moved 10. Merced is one of nine counties that flipped from Trump to the Democrat. Among similar counties, Fresno moved 12 points, Butte 3 and Imperial 32.

Only about 66% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 49,487 votes so far equal 57% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06103.t:
In the race for governor between Becerra and Hilton, Tehama County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 5 points toward the Democrats. Hilton won 14,328 votes to Becerra's 6,585, a margin of R+37, compared with Trump's R+42 in 2024. Only 20,913 votes were cast, about 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

The shift was smaller than California's typical county move of 6 points and well below the state's 11-point swing. Similar Republican counties moved further: Glenn by 6 points, Shasta by 8 and Sutter by 17. Tehama ranked 33rd of 58 California counties by move.

06101.t:
In the race for governor, Sutter County still favored the Republican, Hilton, but by far less than it favored Trump in 2024. With 47% of the expected vote counted, Hilton leads Becerra 9,429 to 7,021, a margin of 15 points, against Trump's 31-point win here. That 17-point move toward the Democrats ranks 11th of California's 58 counties. It is well above the typical county's 6 points and the state's 10. Similar counties barely shifted: Amador did not move, Calaveras moved 1 point and Glenn 4.

Fewer than half the expected ballots are in, so these numbers may still move. The 16,450 votes counted so far equal 42% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06069.t:
San Benito County moved about 11 points toward the Democrats in the race for California governor, where Becerra beat Hilton. Harris carried the county by 13 points in 2024; with partial returns, Becerra leads by 23, 7,964 votes to 4,952. That swing roughly matches the statewide shift of 10 points and is nearly double the typical California county's 6. It ranks 18th of 58 by move. Comparable counties shifted far less: Nevada and San Luis Obispo each moved about 4 points and Mono about 2.

Only 53% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 12,916 ballots so far equal 47% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06005.t:
Amador County did not budge. In the race for governor, Hilton beat Becerra here by 28 points, 12,030 votes to 6,792, the same margin by which Trump beat Harris in 2024. It is one of only four California counties that did not move left: it ranks 55th of 58 by move, while the typical county shifted 6 points toward the Democrats and the state as a whole shifted 10.

Among counties of similar size and 2024 vote, Calaveras was also nearly flat, moving 1 point, but Sutter moved 17 points left and Yuba 10. About 18,822 votes were cast in Amador, 84% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06015.t:

Turnout was 8,249 votes, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Madera County stayed Republican in the race for governor but by far less than in 2024. Trump carried it by 21 points; Hilton won it by 4, 24,269 votes to 22,539 for Becerra. That 17-point swing toward the Democrats ranks 8th of California's 58 counties, well beyond the statewide move of 11 points and the typical county's 6.

Neighbors with a similar 2024 vote split two ways: Tulare and Kings each moved 19 points left, while Tuolumne moved only 3. About 46,808 votes were cast, 86% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06001.t:
In the race for California governor, Alameda County gave Becerra 446,421 votes to Hilton's 105,850, a Democratic margin of 62 points. That is 8 points more Democratic than Harris's 54-point margin here in 2024. The shift is larger than the typical California county's 6 points but smaller than the statewide move of 11 and the typical national move of 14. Among similar counties in the state, San Mateo barely moved, Santa Cruz shifted 4 points and Sonoma 5.

Turnout fell: 552,271 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total. The count cannot tell how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

06025.t:
Imperial County moved further toward the Democrats than any other county in California. Trump carried it by 1 point in 2024 on 54,025 votes; in the race for governor, Becerra leads Hilton by 30 points, 24,068 to 12,932. That 31-point swing is nearly three times the statewide shift of 11 points and far above the typical California county's 6, and it makes Imperial one of 11 counties in the state to flip from Trump to the Democrat. Similar counties moved less: Merced 21 points, Lake 15, Butte 3.

Only 37,000 votes have been counted, about 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 90% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

06027.t:
Inyo County flipped from Trump to the Democrat in the race for governor. Harris lost it by 3 points in 2024; Becerra carried it over Hilton by 5, 3,836 votes to 3,485. That 8-point move toward the Democrats is a little larger than the typical California county's 6 points, but smaller than the state's 10-point shift and well below the typical 14-point move nationally. Inyo was one of nine California counties to switch from a Trump win to a Democratic one.

Turnout was 82% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among counties with similar 2024 results and size, Lake moved 14 points, Imperial 32 and Trinity 3.

06075.t:
In the race for governor, San Francisco gave Becerra 280,594 votes to Hilton's 50,784, a Democratic margin of 69 points, up from Harris's 65-point margin over Trump in 2024. That shift was smaller than California's 11-point move toward the Democrats and below the typical county in the state, which moved about 6 points; San Francisco ranks 35th of 58. Among similar heavily Democratic counties, Alameda moved 8 points left and Santa Cruz 4, while Marin moved 5 points toward the Republicans.

About 331,378 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06029.t:
In the race for governor, Kern County went from a 21-point Trump win in 2024 to a 2-point lead for Becerra over Hilton, 101,516 votes to 97,427. That 23-point move toward the Democrats is the second-largest among California's 58 counties, where the typical county moved 6 points and the state as a whole moved 11. Kern also outpaced the counties most like it. Tulare moved 19 points, Madera 17 and Kings 17, and all three still favored the Republican.

Only 76% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. Votes cast so far equal 70% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06093.t:
In the governor's race, Siskiyou County stayed firmly Republican: Hilton beat Becerra 10,039 to 7,166, a margin of 17 points. That is 3 points narrower than Trump's 19-point win over Harris in 2024, a small move toward the Democrats. Statewide, Becerra won by 31 points, an 11-point swing left from 2024, and the typical California county moved 6 points. Siskiyou ranked 47th of 58 by move.

Its shift matches similar Republican counties nearby. Tuolumne and Mariposa each moved 3 points, Plumas 2. Turnout was 80% of the 2024 vote, 17,205 ballots against 21,489, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06083.t:
Santa Barbara County backed Becerra over Hilton for governor by 33 points, 103,185 votes to 52,116. Harris carried it by 27 in 2024, so the county moved 6 points toward the Democrats. That is exactly the typical move among California's counties and puts it 29th of 58, but it trails the statewide shift of 11 points and the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Solano by 8, Humboldt by 6 and Monterey by 11.

About 155,301 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot show how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

06085.t:
In the governor's race, Santa Clara County voted for Becerra over Hilton 435,779 to 171,780, a Democratic margin of 44 points, up from Harris's 40-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 4-point shift to the left was smaller than the state's 11-point move and the typical California county's 6, ranking 40th of 58. Nationally, the typical county moved 14. Comparable Democratic counties moved a little more: Contra Costa 5 points, Sonoma 4 and Yolo 9.

There were 607,559 votes cast, 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Even so, the county cast the sixth-largest vote in the state.

06045.t:
In the governor's race, Becerra beat Hilton in Mendocino County 20,060 to 10,020, a margin of 33 points. Harris had carried it by 27, so the county moved between 6 and 7 points toward the Democrats. That is close to the typical California county (+6) and to similar counties such as Humboldt and Santa Barbara (both +6), but well short of Monterey (+11), the statewide shift (+11) and the typical county nationally (+14). It ranked 28th of 58 in the state by move.

Only 30,080 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 94% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

06053.t:
In the race for governor, Monterey County backed Becerra over Hilton 87,731 to 36,512, a Democratic margin of 41 points. Harris carried it by 30 in 2024, so the county moved 11 points toward the Democrats. That matches the statewide shift of 11 and is larger than the typical California county's move of 6. Monterey ranked 17th of 58 counties by move. Similar counties moved less: Santa Barbara and Humboldt about 6 points each, Solano 8. Nationally, the typical county moved 14.

Turnout was 124,243 votes, 85% of the 2024 total. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.
